title: Our Place Is Frying Up a Spicy Sale, Including My Favorite Pan
author: Louryn Strampe
text: All products featured on WIRED are independently selected by our editors. However, we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links. Learn more.I’ll sing the praises of Our Place to anyone who will listen. I’ve tried most of its kitchenware, and I have yet to use a product I disliked. Not only do they perform well, but they’re all thoughtfully designed and look great in my kitchen. The only downside is that it can be spendy. Right now, Shop is offering 15 to 30 percent off a huge variety of Our Place kitchenware, and you can get an extra $60 off when you spend $100 or more. This is an excellent way to save on a gift for yourself or someone else.For more home and kitchen deals, check our stories on the Best Black Friday Espresso and Coffee Maker Deals and this great Mustard Made home storage sale.Photograph: Louryn StrampeOur PlaceAlways Pan 2.0$135 $95 (30% off) Shop$135 Amazon$135 $95 (30% off) Our PlaceThe Our Place Always Pan is my number-one kitchen sidekick. I use it nearly every single time I cook because it’s so versatile. The design works well for frying eggs and flipping pancakes, but it’s also deep enough for spaghetti sauce or a quick veggie stir-fry. The nontoxic nonstick coating is still holding up well, though it does stain a bit, which I don’t mind. It’s easy to clean, too. While I think it’s worth $95 regularly, you might want to pick up some accessories to hit that $100 threshold for an extra $60 off. I especially like the Spruce Steamer basket for frozen dumplings and the Egg Poacher to help me hit my protein macros.Courtesy of Our PlaceOur PlaceWonder Oven Pro$325 $275 (15% off) Shop$325 $275 (15% off) Our PlaceI just started testing the Wonder Oven Pro, and I like it so much that I’m considering ditching my microwave. It takes a lot to make me like a countertop appliance given that my apartment kitchen is so tiny, but this sleek little machine has a myriad of functions, from roasting and broiling and baking to dehydrating and even a fancy steam infusion mode (which I have yet to try). The reheat mode is helping me actually eat my leftovers instead of leaving them to die in the fridge. The whole appliance is easy to clean, and the controls are pretty intuitive. If your rental’s appliances are subpar or you just want another multifunction kitchen doodad that works, this is an easy recommendation, especially at its sale price.Power up with unlimited access to WIRED.
